evidence:
Frozen inputs: all 32 files in manifest.json match their sha256 values, and no extra file is present. All 6 raw-evidence-index artifacts match their sha256 values. I re-derived each fact in the staged-task-contract cross-file table.

(1) PORT 3000. Stated in integration.md:3 ('listen on 0.0.0.0 port 3000'). Matches test.sh:48,104-109 (PORT="3000", probes 127.0.0.1:3000), the restart helper heredoc at test.sh:136,164, the opening line of every prompt.md (http://localhost:3000), app_context.md:4, and server.js:13,519 (listen(PORT, "0.0.0.0")).

(2) Entry /app/server.js. Stated in instruction.md:5 and integration.md:3. Matches test.sh:68,97 and solve.sh, which copies solution/app into /app.

(3) Database. integration.md:3 says '/app/app.db, or at the path in DB_PATH'. test.sh:98-101,109 passes DB_PATH=/app/app.db, or the copy path when /app is not writable. The restart helper uses the same __APP_DB__ (test.sh:165,189). server.js:14 honours DB_PATH and defaults to __dirname/app.db.

(4) Seed. instruction.md:5 and integration.md:5 name /assets/seed_data.json. task.toml artifacts = ["/app", "/assets"] and environment/Dockerfile:15 copies assets/. environment/assets/seed_data.json is byte-identical to solution/app/seed/seed_data.json (sha f69616e2...). server.js:29 reads the copy in /app first and falls back to /assets.

(5) Clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z. Stated in integration.md:7. Matches seed clock at line 2, app_context.md:27, functional criteria deleted_and_expired Part B, sent_once_in_order Part B and search_and_transcript B1 ('2026-05-12 11:00'), and server.js:32 (CLOCK = seed.clock, also used for the transcript's generated time). I recomputed every relative-date claim against the seed:
- K-1 sent 05-01 on the 7-day M-11: gone. Replies K-14 and held K-15 survive.
- K-10 at 05-05T11:00:00Z is exactly 7 days old: gone. K-11, one second later: kept.
- K-13 ('4 May', 8 days 2 hours old, so the 'eight-day-old' in timer_changes holds) is deleted by a 7-day timer. Held K-7 survives.
- K-17 'sent 3 May' is held and overdue, so it disappears on release.
- K-8 (05-10) survives the temporary 7-day M-13 timer, so message_links and live_updates can still use it.

(6) Accounts and password. walls-and-retention.md:3-15 lists 5 accounts with password123. These match seed accounts (names and roles), app_context.md:8-16, server.js:17, and every account used in a criterion. The annotations in app_context (Gwen M-11 and M-13, Paul M-12, Dev walled from M-12, Harriet with partner powers) match the seed's client and walled fields and the note's partner-only rules.

(7) Judge and model. They appear only in task.toml [verifier.env] (claude-code and z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx, frozen block intact). The 5 judge.toml files each carry only the judge = "claude-code" fallback.

(8) Shares. scoring.toml is byte-identical to the template: gates 0.0/0.0, weights 0.6/0.2/0.2, floor 0.05. score.py is template-identical. No judge.toml has a [judge] weight.

(9) Restart helper variable. test.sh:193 exports APP_RESTART_HELPER. functional/judge.toml:27 passes the literal "$APP_RESTART_HELPER", which rewardkit 0.1.7 agents.py:66 expands with os.path.expandvars. restart_mcp.py exposes the restart_app tool. Its single-use marker (helper.name + '.used') matches test.sh:192, which removes app-restart.sh.used. functional/prompt.md:61-66 and the persistence criterion name restart_app on the 'verifier' server, which matches the judge.toml server name.

(10) Quoted counts. task.toml description and provenance quote no criterion count. The functional/judge.toml:9 comment '16 x 550 + 900 + 900 = 10600 s' within the 11100 s scored budget is correct:
- there are 16 [[criterion]] blocks;
- polish and visual timeout = 900;
- the scored budget is 11100 at test.sh:224;
- gates are 600 + 600 within 1500 at test.sh:213.
The judge.toml:10 claim that the 'template default is batched/9000' matches the template's functional/judge.toml.

(11) Literals. A script compared every quoted seed-like literal in all judge.toml files and app_context against the seed: 32 of 32 match exactly, including the case-variant 'survey BOOKED' and the misspelt earlier version 'notice recieved'. Product literals in the criteria ('edited', 'On hold', 'new messages', 'not available', timers off/1/7/30) match the brief (conversations.md:9,23-25; walls-and-retention.md:17,23,29) and the seed's timer_options_days. Matter titles and the firm name ('Kittle & Rowe') agree across instruction, seed, app_context and the render gate. The template-controlled files (test.sh, Dockerfiles, .dockerignore, solve.sh, score.py, restart_mcp.py, scoring.toml) are byte-identical to the frozen template. task.toml differs only in the task-specific fields.

(12) Golden run. The hash-verified scripted golden run (functional-before.json and functional-after.json, not a configured judge run) reports all 16 functional checks, gate_constraints and polish_refusal_in_place as true. This is consistent with the criteria literals applied to the golden.

Adversarial probes, none of which exposed a drift:
- A broken app that hard-codes a seed path under cwd crashes under test.sh, because it starts from an arbitrary cwd. integration.md:3 warns about exactly this.
- A conforming app that reads only /assets/seed_data.json, uses PORT or a fixed 3000, writes 'Not available.' or 'not available', or picks any route is accepted. Both the verifier environment and the prompts allow it: /assets is an artifact, and prompts say 'any endpoint path' and 'observable outcomes rather than exact wording'.

Non-blocking notes, which are not drifts:
- The criteria allow 'within about ten seconds' where conversations.md:31 says 'about five seconds' and walls-and-retention.md:19 says 'a few seconds'. This tolerance is lenient, so a brief-conforming app still passes.
- The visual prompt's 0-5 anchors coexist with rewardkit Likert points=5, which normalizes (raw-1)/4 clamped (models.py:47). Anchors 0 and 1 both score 0.0, and the prompt's 'an integer from 1 to 5' literal is accurate. Scale design belongs to row 41.
- During this review a transient 'grep.exe.stackdump' briefly appeared in the frozen task cache directory. It was absent from the manifest and gone on re-listing, and it is not in projects/kittle-matter-chat. It was a concurrent tool crash artefact, not a task file (row 50 owner may confirm).
